subject: Cloudly integration - telemetry, auth & SDK follow-up
messages:
From: Mike Chen <mike@cloudly.io>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudly.io
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood integration — post-demo questions

Avery / team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — it was helpful. I pulled together the post-call questions from engineering and procurement below so we can triage before the technical deep dive. Attaching a short doc with our integration requirements (redwood_integration_req.pdf).

1) Auth & SDK
 - Do you support API keys + short-lived tokens? We prefer rotating keys via our KMS and would like mTLS for the private deployment option.
 - Language SDKs: we primarily use Node (server), Go for some services, and Python for ML jobs. Do you have sample snippets for auth flows?

2) Routing / rollout
 - We want to route a % of requests to a smaller cheaper variant during canary (same API surface). How are model variants addressed in requests and can we set per-route fallbacks?

3) Structured output / tool-calling
 - We need predictable structured output for post-processing (JSON schema enforcement) and support for tool-calls (external HTTP/webhook invocations). Any recommended patterns?

4) Embeddings & reranker
 - We'll index documents in our vector DB (Milvus) and want to run an on-request reranker that takes top-K and returns final ranking. Is there an embeddings + rerank orchestration you recommend?

5) Observability / telemetry
 - Important: correlate user request across our services and Redwood. Do you propagate a trace id header? Do you emit token-level latency breakdowns in response headers? Which log fields should we expect in platform logs for debugging (model, tokens, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, quantization)?
 - Do you have a sample dashboard or Hints for our SLOs (p50/p95 per route) and how telemetry maps to billing?

Procurement notes:
 - We also need an outline SOW and procurement items for our legal team.

Happy to jump on a technical call if it helps.

—Mike
Mike Chen
CTO, Cloudly Inc.
<mike@cloudly.io>

Mike — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and a proposal for next steps (technical kickoff + procurement sync). I attached a minimal curl snippet and examples (example-curl.txt) — will follow up with a short SDK gist before the call.

Quick answers:
- Auth & SDK: We support API keys with short-lived exchange tokens (rotate via customer KMS). For Private deployments we offer mTLS + customer-managed KMS. SDKs: Node/Go/Python are supported; I can send language-specific auth flows.

- Routing & rollouts: Model variants are addressed by model_id in the request body and we have route-level policies. You can specify a routing policy that does percent-based traffic splitting to variants; automatic fallback to a compatible variant is supported if capacity is constrained.

- Structured output & tool calling: We recommend a schema-first response validator in the prompt and function/tool calling (we surface structured tool-call events). For deterministic outputs we also recommend response sampling constraints + a post-parse validation step; we have a rollout example in the shared doc.

- Embeddings & reranker: Typical pattern: embeddings -> vector DB (Milvus) -> candidate retrieval -> rerank via a second model call (we support embedding generation + a low-latency reranker model). We can provide an example where the reranker accepts the top-50 and returns scores.

- Observability: We surface an optional request header (X-Redwood-Req-Id) that we echo in logs and responses. We also expose a header with latency breakdown (X-Redwood-Latency: kernel=12ms;kv_cache=3ms;network=5ms). Platform logs include fields: request_id, user_id (if provided), model_id, token_count, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, quantization_profile, and node_region. We'll share a draft of a recommended dashboard.

Next steps:
1) Technical deep dive (engineering working session) — propose Wed 11/10 10:00–11:00 PT.
2) I'll loop in our infra lead for an auth/mTLS checklist.
3) I'll drop a HubSpot note and an integration doc (link below) + SOW draft.

Links:
 - Integration doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-cloudly-redwood-integration
 - HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/CLD-12345

If that schedule works I’ll book time and send an agenda.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Cloudly integration — telemetry, auth proposals

Forwarding our reply + my suggested observability proposal. I think we should be explicit about the headers and log fields so Cloudly can wire their tracing. Draft notes below (attaching obs-proposal.md).

Suggested observability contract
- Trace correlation:
  - Ingress header: X-Cloudly-Req-Id (passed from Cloudly) and X-Redwood-Req-Id (generated/returned by Redwood). We echo any incoming trace id into logs and the response.
  - We should recommend Cloudly propagate a single header (X-Trace-Id) across internal services; Redwood will accept and echo it.

- Response headers for quick diagnostics:
  - X-Redwood-Req-Id: string (always present)
  - X-Redwood-Latency: semi-colon list (kernel=##ms;kv_cache=##ms;network=##ms;total=##ms)
  - X-Redwood-Model: model_id/version (for quick routing diagnosis)

- Log/trace fields we will include in platform logs (and send via forwarding):
  - request_id, trace_id (if provided), user_id (opt), model_id, model_version, token_count, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, batch_size, kv_cache_hit (true/false), quantization_profile, node_region, node_id, inference_time_ms, queued_time_ms

- Sampling & retention:
  - Default: full logs for errors and 1% sampling for success paths; can increase for dedicated customers.

- Metrics/dashboards to provide:
  - Per-route: p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, error rate, cost per 1k tokens
  - Model-level kernel timings (GPU kernel time vs CPU pre/post processing)

SDK snippet suggestion (pseudo-Node):
  const res = await redwood.call({
    model: 'rwd-llama-70b-v1',
    input: prompt,
    headers: { 'X-Cloudly-Req-Id': traceId }
  })

We should confirm exact field names with engineering, but this gives Cloudly a concrete contract to wire into their tracing system.

If we agree I can convert the notes into a short one-page observability SLA to include in the SOW.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Attachment: obs-proposal.md (text/markdown)
